insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (refer Policy Schedule)

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.reference: Section D (Waiting Period & Exclusions) > Standard General Exclusions & Waiting Period > 1. Pre-existing Diseases (Excl01), Page 11-12
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage. Claims for PED treatment become payable only after you complete 3 years on the policy without a break.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy with us.
good.reference: Section D > 2. Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period (Excl02), Page 12
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. You can claim for these only after completing 2 years on the policy.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days from the policy start date, except if the claim arises due to an accident. This is a standard waiting period that can affect claims soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: The Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred in the 30 days immediately before You were Hospitalized
good.reference: Section C > 2. Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses, Page 11
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred in the 30 days immediately before hospitalization are covered if related to the hospitalization. This helps pay for tests and consultations leading up to admission.

good.name: Cashless Network
good.quote: We may provide Cashless facility for Hospitalization expenses either directly or through the Third Party Administrator (TPA) if treatment is undergone at a  Network Hospital
good.reference: Section F > I. Claims Procedure > 2. Cashless Facility for Hospitalization, Page 24
good.explanation: Cashless treatment may be provided when you take treatment at a network hospital, either directly or through a TPA. Since it says "may provide" and does not specify the network size, availability can vary by hospital and insurer arrangements.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: All person(s) named in the Schedule to this Policy above the age of 80 years (age last birthday) shall bear a co-pay of 10% for each and every claim.
bad.reference: Section D (Waiting Period & Exclusions) > II. Specific Exclusions > 2. Co-payment, Page 15
bad.explanation: For insured persons above age 80, a 10% co-pay applies on each and every claim. This means you must pay 10% of the admissible bill amount from your pocket every time you claim.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: In the event of a claim being admitted under this Policy, the Sum Insured for the remaining Policy Period shall stand correspondingly reduced by the amount of claim paid (including ‘taxes’) or admitted and shall be reckoned accordingly.
bad.reference: Section B > Specific Definitions > Def 6 Sum Insured, Page 9
bad.explanation: Sum insured reduces during the policy year by the amount of claim paid/admitted (including taxes). No automatic restore/reinstatement is mentioned, so a large claim can significantly reduce cover for the rest of the year.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Non-Medical expenses such as Food charges (other than patient’s diet provided by hospital), laundry charges, attendant charges, ambulance collar, ambulance equipment, baby food, baby utility charges etc. Full list of Non -Medical expenses is attached
bad.reference: Section D > II. Specific Exclusions > 15, Page 15 and Annexure I (List of Non-Medical Expenses), Page 32 onwards
bad.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items (like attendant charges, laundry, baby food/utility charges, etc.) are excluded as per the attached list. These costs can add up during hospitalization and will be out-of-pocket.

bad.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
bad.quote: The Post Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred in the 60 days immediately after You were discharged
bad.reference: Section C > 3. Post Hospitalization Medical Expenses, Page 11
bad.explanation: Medical expenses incurred in the 60 days immediately after discharge are covered if related to the hospitalization. Coverage beyond 60 days is not included, which can be limiting for longer recoveries.

bad.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
bad.reference: Section D > II. Specific Exclusions > 1, Page 15
bad.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization expenses are listed under specific exclusions, indicating home-based treatment is not covered. If hospital admission is not possible and treatment is taken at home, the claim may be rejected.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: Room Rent means the amount charged by a Hospital towards Room and Boarding expenses and shall include the Associated Medical Expenses
unclear.reference: Section B > Standard Definitions > Def 42 Room Rent, Page 8
unclear.explanation: Only the definition of room rent is provided, without stating any eligible room category or limit in this extract. The actual room rent entitlement (and whether proportionate deductions can apply) would depend on the schedule/benefit table.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
